description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 18, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: earendil-works/pi is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: earendil-works/pi leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: earendil-works/pi — 13 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 5.7 below its current daily pace, with 21 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 104 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
andrewyng/openworker — No same-day commit after 41 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Pi can store the wait while the host supplies the wakeup
dailyInsight.insight: Pi’s experimental durable harness has merged sleeping task state and a host wake contract. The inspected changelog still lists the change as unreleased after v1.3.0.
dailyInsight.mechanism: A sleep commits an absolute deadline and next checkpoint, ending its invocation. With onWake configured, a host alarm resumes due work; the default Node timer instead keeps the process alive.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Integrators can design delayed or polling work that survives process eviction, but adoption includes host alarm ownership and a storage compatibility change.

actions.audience: Builders embedding Pi’s durable harness in an evictable host
actions.label: Prepare one delayed-task trial on disposable storage
actions.instruction: Wait for a containing release, then copy a test dataset and verify a stored deadline across eviction, alarm-driven resumption and a retry-safe external action. Keep the original database untouched: the new SQLite schema cannot reopen under v1.3.0 or earlier.
actions.effort: One bounded integration trial when a containing release is available

receipts.title: Persisted sleeping tasks and host wake contract
receipts.supports: Ends sleeping invocations while preserving a checkpoint and deadline; reports runnable work and the earliest sleep to the host.

receipts.title: Workerd eviction and alarm coverage
receipts.supports: Adds tests of stored sleep through eviction and scripted turn recovery, and declines background timers that prevent eviction.

receipts.title: Unreleased migration and API boundary
receipts.supports: Places the change after v1.3.0 and documents SQLite rollback incompatibility and older JSONL readers not resuming sleeping tasks.

confidence.basis: Pinned implementation, earlier checkpoints, followup corrections, migration and workerd test definitions inspected.

dailyInsight.limitation: Tests were inspected, not executed here; their model is scripted and clock advanced manually. No live cloud completion, billing reduction or exactly-once external effect is established.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A containing release changes the wake contract, or a pinned host integration cannot preserve the deadline and resume the task after eviction despite a correctly armed alarm.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A containing release and a real delayed-task trial across host eviction with retry-safe external effects.
